title: Agentic Engineering: Working With AI, Not Just Using It — Brendan O'Leary
talk_summary: Brendan O'Leary argues AI coding agents should be treated like fast but context-blind junior engineers, so engineers must curate context, separate research/planning from implementation, and review agent work like PRs. He gives concrete practices: keep context under control, use AGENTS.md and on-demand skills, disable unused MCPs, and route implementation to cheaper models after a strong plan.

takeaways.what_they_do: Persist state outside the context window, load only relevant files/tools, compress or summarize after debugging, and start a new session when the agent goes off track.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The quality can degrade as you get over about 50% full.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a research-only mode that cannot edit, produce a reviewed research doc, then a plan file with scope/files/tests, then implement in a fresh session.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a bad line of research can potentially be hundreds of lines of bad code.

takeaways.what_they_do: After the plan is fixed, the implementation session gets only the plan; the speaker says this lets a smaller, faster, or cheaper model execute it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use maybe a smaller, faster, or cheaper model to implement it because we've spent the time in the research and plan phase

takeaways.what_they_do: AGENTS.md is the always-loaded minimal project rulebook; skills are reusable playbooks loaded only for specific recurring workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your project has an agents.md with a minimal amount of information that an agent needs to know about

takeaways.what_they_do: Each MCP adds tool descriptions to the system prompt on every call, so unused servers waste tokens and can confuse the agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you're not actually using that, to disable it

takeaways.technique: Isolate agent work and review as PR
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep agent work isolated in worktrees/PRs, commit frequently, and review agent output like a junior engineer's pull request; human time is highest leverage at research/plan.
takeaways.evidence_quote: isolate your work from the agent's work, and then review that agent's work as a pull request
